reviewed_version: Publisher version of record, 41 pages, FoCM 26 (2026) 2165–2205, online 13 August 2025
paper_title: Improved global performance guarantees of second-order methods in convex minimization
summary: Two Major issues invalidate the claimed feasibility rate and its direct LP transfer. Six Minor groups identify clipped-step, signed-lemma, local-scaling, index-cost, nondegeneracy and cubic-parameter corrections while explicitly preserving the unaffected conditional conclusions.

problems.title: The feasibility application discards an essential diameter logarithm
problems.location: Section 4.2, p. 2185, compared with Theorem 6 and (44)
problems.check: For F(x)=-log(1-x^2) on [-1,1], nu=2,A=1,b=1-epsilon, the dual inverse Hessian is s(s+1), s=sqrt(1+y^2). PFS increments obey |dy|<=(beta+gamma)(|y|+2). Reaching lambda<=1/2 requires y>=1/(4epsilon), so k>=log(1+1/(8epsilon))/log(1+beta+gamma).
problems.result: This analytic Omega(log(1/epsilon)) lower bound contradicts the uniform ordinary O(sqrt(nu log(1/epsilon))) claim for fixed nu. D is at least y_star/sqrt(2)=Theta(1/epsilon).
problems.correction: Retain and estimate the diameter logarithm before asserting a feasibility rate or superiority over long-step schemes. Revise the associated contribution and convergence discussion.
problems.counterevidence: Theorem 6 with its full logarithm is not refuted. The independent numerical runs corroborate, but do not replace, the analytic lower bound.

independent_check.source_claim: Section 4.2 item 2 asserts ordinary O(sqrt(nu log(1/epsilon))) for the specified PFS by citing (44), and uses that to assert improved dependence on depth.
operative_assumptions_verified: The exact publisher VoR uses ordinary O, not a logarithm-suppressing notation.
The interval barrier has positive Hessian, an attained analytic center at zero, F(0)=0, full-row-rank A=1, and valid fixed barrier parameter nu=2.
For each 0<epsilon<=1/4, the specified dual f=F*-b*y is globally smooth with positive Hessian and an attained minimum; f' has negative and positive limiting signs at minus and plus infinity.
Under the corrected depth domain [0,1], the depth of b=1-epsilon in [-1,1] is exactly epsilon.
independent_check.decisive_independent_reasoning: Independently differentiated F=-log(1-a^2), checked the barrier inequalities, conjugate a(y)=y/(1+sqrt(1+y^2)), and f''(y)=1/[s(s+1)]. The minimizer is y*=2b/(1-b^2), Delta=F(b)=Theta(log(1/epsilon)), and D>=y*/sqrt(2)=Theta(1/epsilon). From the actual PFS centered update, |dy|sqrt(f'')<=beta+gamma=0.1385; therefore |y_k|+2<=2(1+beta+gamma)^k. Lambda<=1/2 requires a>=1-2epsilon and hence y>=(1-2epsilon)/(2epsilon(1-epsilon))>=1/(4epsilon). Thus k>=log(1+1/(8epsilon))/log(1+beta+gamma)=Omega(log(1/epsilon)). This contradicts the claimed uniform square-root-log rate for fixed nu, independently of the tightness of Theorem 6.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_limits: Theorem 6 with the full diameter logarithm is not refuted. No lower bound for all feasibility algorithms is asserted. The five old 100-digit PFS trajectories and their centering residuals were hash-verified and parsed, not rerun by this executor; they corroborate the analytic argument.
independent_check.severity_reason: A claimed core feasibility complexity improvement and its depth-rate comparison are materially false on a family satisfying the real assumptions. Whole-paper failure is not required for Major.
independent_check.repair_check: Retaining the logarithm is necessary. A replacement uniform feasibility theorem or corrected full asymptotic upper bound is not established here.

problems.title: The zero-gap LP embedding does not satisfy positive feasibility depth
problems.check: The homogeneous equalities imply x^T s=tau*(c^T x+b^T s1-tau*b^T c1)=0. Thus no point has all x,s,tau positive. For min x subject to x=1,x>=0, the normalized solution is (x,s,tau)=(1/2,0,1/2). A=[1,0],b=1,c=0 additionally admits the tau=0 ray x=(0,1),s=0.
problems.result: Eliminating the simplex equality does not create an interior feasible point, and nonzero homogeneous solutions need not have tau>0. The claimed direct LP complexity transfer is unsupported.
problems.correction: Provide a strictly feasible perturbation or embedding with an explicit positive-depth bound and correct extraction rules; otherwise remove the claimed direct transfer.
problems.counterevidence: This is not a claim that established homogeneous self-dual methods fail. It concerns the particular zero-gap construction and hypotheses printed here.

independent_check.source_claim: The displayed homogeneous zero-gap LP system, intersected with the simplex, is claimed to inherit the preceding positive-depth feasibility complexity.
operative_assumptions_verified: Used the actual full-row-rank block form A=(I,B), with all printed homogeneous equalities, nonnegativity and unit-simplex normalization.
The scalar LP example has a finite attained optimum; the tau=0 example has a feasible original LP.
independent_check.decisive_independent_reasoning: Set y=tau*c1-s1. The equations give Ax=tau*b, A^T*y+s=tau*c and c^T*x+b^T*s1-tau*b^T*c1=0. Multiplying yields x^T*s=tau*(c^T*x-b^T*y)=0. No feasible point can have every x and s coordinate strictly positive; eliminating the simplex equality or translating its center cannot produce a positive-depth feasible point. For min x subject to x=1,x>=0 the only normalized triple is (1/2,0,1/2). Separately A=(1,0),b=1,c=(0,0),x=(0,1),s=(0,0),tau=0 satisfies the printed homogeneous system and normalization but cannot be dehomogenized.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_limits: Established homogeneous self-dual algorithms are not challenged. A separate perturbation or properly augmented embedding could supply different hypotheses, but none is supplied by the printed direct reduction.
independent_check.severity_reason: The hypothesis required for the claimed direct LP transfer fails identically for the displayed construction, materially damaging a central application.
independent_check.repair_check: The need for strict feasibility, a depth estimate and case-correct solution extraction is established. No replacement LP embedding is claimed to have been constructed or validated.
independent_check.check_origin_note: Source reading, analytic reasoning and counterevidence assessment are current-executor work. Existing numerical receipts retain their original execution origin; only missing repair/hypothesis checks were newly executed in focused_validation.py.

problems.title: The predictor and clipped path parameter in (75) are inconsistent
problems.check: For f=x^2/2+x^4/4,M_f=1,x=x0=100/2497,t=1, H0=(2503/2497)^2, gamma=.158, the input centering residual is zero and t_plus=0. The full predictor and Newton corrector give lambda_f(x_plus)=0.003121087486...>beta=.0015; the violation was checked with exact rational squares.
problems.result: The unconditional centering statement of Theorem 8 is false when t is clipped.
problems.correction: Set tau=min(t,gamma/(M_f||grad f(x0)||*_x)), use y=x-tau H_x^-1 grad f(x0), and t_plus=t-tau. Define zero-gradient termination and the local phase.
problems.counterevidence: Clipping under the centering condition implies M_f lambda_f(x)<=gamma+beta=.1595<1/2, so this defect does not refute the first-entry complexity in Theorems 9–10. Minor calibration is based on this limited impact.

independent_check.source_claim: Equation (75) clips the path parameter at zero while retaining the full predictor displacement; Theorem 8 asserts unconditional centering of the resulting step.
operative_assumptions_verified: The quartic is globally self-concordant with maximum normalized third-derivative ratio 2/3, so M_f=1 is admissible.
At x=x0=100/2497 and t=1, the path residual is exactly zero and sqrt(H)=2503/2497; gamma=79/500 and beta=3/2000 are the printed constants.
The full proposed parameter decrement exceeds t, so the actual clipped branch is exercised.
independent_check.decisive_independent_reasoning: Reviewed the exact rational counterexample and independently traced the predictor/Newton formulas: y=x-gamma/sqrt(H), x_plus=2*y^3/(1+3*y^2), with lambda(x_plus)=0.003121087486...>0.0015. The missing repair was checked using the same clipped tau in both predictor and t_plus: this gives a residual about 4.1793e-12. The uniform repaired centering estimate for q<=gamma is about 0.001475674<beta.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_limits: The centering hypothesis and clipping imply M_f*lambda_f(x)<=beta+gamma=0.1595<1/2. The problematic continuation starts inside the target region. Therefore the example does not refute first-entry complexity in Theorems 9-10.
independent_check.severity_reason: The unconditional theorem and post-entry continuation need correction, but the central first-entry bound is not invalidated by this defect. This impact limitation, not the length of the repair, supports Minor.
independent_check.repair_check: Clip tau=min(t,gamma/(M_f*||g0||*_x)) in both formulas and stop or handle a zero initial gradient before division; local clipped centering checked.

problems.title: The signed predictor lemma and dual parameter substitution use inconsistent signs
problems.check: Quartic f=x^2/2+x^4/4, M_f=2/3,x=1,t=0,c=4,h=1,r=2,tau=-1/10 satisfies |tau|M_f r<1 but gives lambda_next=1.09555... while the printed right side is 261/289=0.90311.... In Lemma 7, the residual Phi'-tb transported along +H^-1 b requires t+tau, not t-tau.
problems.result: Lemma 4 is false for negative tau as written; Lemma 7's intermediate comparison uses the wrong path label.
problems.correction: Use absolute tau in the bound or restrict to nonnegative tau and reverse the direction consistently. Replace the dual comparison label by t(u)+tau.
problems.counterevidence: The intended positive-step bound and Lemma 7's centering conclusion survive these repairs. The interval-conjugate check confirms the erroneous intermediate bound, not failure of the corrected dual method.

independent_check.decision: Upheld within sign and intermediate-comparison scope
independent_check.source_claim: Lemma 4 asserts its signed-step bound for |tau|M_f*r<1 without absolute values in the bound; Lemma 7 substitutes a dual path label with the wrong sign.
operative_assumptions_verified: The quartic example uses admissible M_f=2/3, x=1,t=0,c=4,h=1,r=2,tau=-1/10, and satisfies the stated small-step condition.
For Lemma 7, Phi_t=Phi-t<b,u> is the actual convention; the interval conjugate is a legitimate nondegenerate dual example.
independent_check.decisive_independent_reasoning: The squared residual in the negative-tau example is 4116841/3430000, whereas the printed upper bound is 261/289<1; the inequality is false. Applying the positive-step lemma with c'=-c,t'=-t,tau'=-tau preserves the objective and point and supplies the absolute-tau repair; the repaired example bound is 201/169 and is sufficient. For Phi_t=Phi-t<b,u>, a +tau*H^-1*b predictor transports the residual to t(u)+tau. The old exact/numerical check has wrong-label residual about 0.523711 above 0.115928, while the correct-label residual is about 0.008065.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_limits: The intended positive-step predictor bound survives. In the one-dimensional dual example the minimized residual lambda(v) is zero, so the counterexample concerns the intermediate comparison, not a false corrected centering conclusion.
independent_check.severity_reason: The unsupported signed extension and path-label error are localized; the actual positive-step algorithm and repaired centering conclusion are not shown to fail.
independent_check.repair_check: Absolute tau follows by a symmetry reduction, or restrict to nonnegative tau. Under the minus-linear dual convention use t(u)+tau, equivalently parameter -t(u) in the plus-linear lemma.

problems.title: Newton and distance formulas need their local and scaling qualifications
problems.location: Equation (11), p. 2170; Theorem 1, p. 2172; surrounding definitions
problems.check: Theorem 1 lacks M_f lambda<1. For the global standard self-concordant quartic at x=10, lambda>50 and lambda_after_Newton>25, whereas its displayed right side is <(50/49)^2. In (11), the last fraction must have numerator lambda, not M_f lambda; f=x^2/2,M_f=1/2,x=1/5 gives distance 1/5>printed bound 1/9.
problems.result: The unqualified Newton inequality and the expanded scaled-distance expression are false.
problems.correction: State M_f lambda<1; retain lambda/(1-M_f lambda). Treat M_f=0 as the quadratic case or use a positive admissible constant, define omega-star on [0,1), and terminate at zero residual.
problems.counterevidence: The first omega-star derivative expression in (11) is correct. Intended small-decrement uses of Theorem 1 remain valid; the DNM (22) proof was not refuted.

independent_check.decision: Upheld as local and scaling qualification
independent_check.source_claim: Theorem 1 displays the Newton estimate without M_f*lambda<1; the last expansion in (11) has an extra M_f.
operative_assumptions_verified: The surrounding discussion describes local convergence; that context limits the intended application but does not make the unqualified displayed inequality true.
The quartic with M_f=1 is globally self-concordant. A positive definite quadratic admits any positive self-concordance constant.
independent_check.decisive_independent_reasoning: For the quartic at x=10 the Newton point is 2000/301, lambda(x)>50 and lambda(x_plus)>25, while the displayed rational right side is below (50/49)^2. Independently differentiated omega_star: (1/M_f)*omega_star'(M_f*lambda)=lambda/(1-M_f*lambda). For f=x^2/2,M_f=1/2,x=1/5, the actual distance 1/5 exceeds the printed final fraction 1/9; the corrected expression is 2/9.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_limits: The first derivative expression in (11) is correct. Restoring the small-decrement condition preserves its intended local uses; no failure of the damped-Newton argument or of the externally cited theorem under its proper assumptions is alleged.
independent_check.severity_reason: These are localized domain/scaling specifications; the intended local convergence regime remains available.
independent_check.repair_check: State M_f*lambda<1, use numerator lambda, handle M_f=0/quadratic and zero residual separately, and use the real omega_star domain [0,1).
independent_check.check_origin_note: Source reading, analytic reasoning and counterevidence assessment are current-executor work. Existing numerical receipts retain their original execution origin; only missing repair/hypothesis checks were newly executed in focused_validation.py.

problems.title: Finite-iteration indices, constants and work counts need correction
problems.location: Theorems 5 and 9; Remark 2 and (43); Remark 3; adaptive PFS; rho after (83)
problems.check: Products for t_N contain N updates, not N+1. At f=x^2/2,M_f=1,x0=1,N=0, (43) says 1<=0.99319375. The specified PFS constant is 17.14198257, not <=17.1. The rho expression needs plus gamma^2/(1-gamma)^2; its corrected margin stays positive. Each adaptive iteration evaluates i_k+1 trial Newton steps.
problems.result: Several literal finite estimates and counts are incorrect, although the corrected principal nonlocal arguments and orders survive.
problems.correction: Use sum k=0..N-1 for t_N, or t_(N+1) with N+1 terms; change 'minimum' to 'maximum' in the concave argument, correct rounding and rho sign, count accepted trials, and distinguish outer iterations from Hessian evaluations.
problems.counterevidence: The source image shows a sum of logarithms, not a product; the extraction ambiguity is explicitly rejected. Corrected PCPFS constant is 13.43493615 and centering margins remain admissible.

independent_check.source_claim: Finite-index products, a concave allocation extremum, numerical constants, the rho formula and adaptive work counts have literal inconsistencies.
operative_assumptions_verified: The product from t0 to tN has N updates.
The source image contains a sum of logarithms, not a product.
The beta/gamma constants and trial-index convention are those actually printed.
independent_check.decisive_independent_reasoning: Use sums through N-1 for tN, or t(N+1) for N+1 terms; the N-squared order survives. At f=x^2/2,M_f=1,x0=1,N=0, (43) gives 1<=0.99319375 although the applicable initial conditions hold. For log(1-h/d), the second derivative is -h*(2*d-h)/(d^2*(d-h)^2)<0 on d>h>0, so equal allocation maximizes the sum. The printed PFS constants give 17.14198257, not <=17.1. Substituting the plus sign required by (82) yields a positive rho margin 0.024704621, kappa=0.035064827 and PCPFS constant 13.43493615. Trials indexed 0..i_k cost i_k+1, giving 2(k+1)+log2(gamma_-1/gamma_k). PCPFS outer iterations use two Hessian evaluations versus one for PFS.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_limits: The product-of-logarithms interpretation is rejected using the source image. Corrected nonlocal rates, admissible centering margins and positive-decrease reasoning remain intact. A smaller outer-iteration constant alone is not a runtime comparison.
independent_check.severity_reason: Literal finite bounds, counts and constants need correction without demonstrated loss of the corrected principal asymptotic orders.
independent_check.repair_check: Index endpoints, concavity direction, rounding, rho plus sign, accepted-trial counts and comparison unit were independently checked.

problems.title: Feasibility depth and dual problem data need explicit nondegeneracy conditions
problems.check: Since 0 lies in int Q, arbitrarily large delta>1 makes (1-delta)Q contain any fixed feasible point; the unrestricted maximum in (56) is unbounded. Dual Hessian A H^-1 A^T is singular unless A has full row rank; B=(1,0),c=(1,0),Q=[-1,1]^2 gives dependent rows A=(-c^T;B).
problems.result: Some definitions and inverses are not meaningful for the stated general data.
problems.correction: Use delta in [0,1], retain the source's explicit analytic-center assumption as a scope restriction, remove redundant consistent constraints, treat constant objectives/zero directions separately, define Phi_t(u)=Phi(u)-t<b,u>, and use sigma>0 for reciprocal certificates.
problems.counterevidence: Section 4.2 already assumes an analytic center at zero and F(0)=0. The no-analytic-center barrier is outside that scope and is not an additional defect; the report was narrowed accordingly. The Major interval example has a genuine analytic center, full rank and a nonzero direction.

independent_check.decision: Core depth/rank findings upheld; analytic-center allegation narrowed to scope clarification
independent_check.source_claim: The depth maximum in (56) allows delta>=0 without an upper endpoint, and subsequent dual formulas require invertible Hessians and nonzero denominators.
operative_assumptions_verified: Section 4.2 explicitly assumes grad F(0)=0 and F(0)=0. Analytic-center existence is an operative source assumption, not an omitted assumption.
The global method also assumes a nondegenerate Hessian; a data reduction is necessary before applying it to a rank-deficient dual.
The Major interval-barrier construction satisfies the analytic-center, full-rank and nonzero-direction requirements.
independent_check.decisive_independent_reasoning: If B(0,r) lies in Q and delta>1, the reflected dilation (1-delta)Q contains B(0,(delta-1)r). Every fixed feasible point therefore belongs to it for all sufficiently large delta, so the unrestricted maximum is unbounded; [0,1] is the intended depth domain. Since H is positive definite, A*H^-1*A^T is invertible exactly when A has full row rank. B=(1,0), c=(1,0) in Q=[-1,1]^2 gives dependent rows A=(-c^T;B) and a constant objective on Bx=0. Reciprocal sigma certificates and normalized zero directions need their stated positivity/termination domains.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_limits: The barrier -log(1+x) on (-1,infinity) has no analytic center and thus violates the paper's explicit analytic-center assumption. It is not a counterexample under that assumption. The report and findings were corrected accordingly. No new Major issue is inferred from removable redundant constraints or already-solved cases.
independent_check.severity_reason: Depth-domain and data-preprocessing specifications are local qualifications. The analytic-center discussion contributes no additional established defect.
independent_check.repair_check: Restrict delta to [0,1], preserve the existing analytic-center scope, reduce redundant consistent rows/handle constant objectives, use scalar Phi-t<b,u>, require sigma>0 in reciprocals, and handle zero directions.
independent_check.check_origin_note: Source reading, analytic reasoning and counterevidence assessment are current-executor work. Existing numerical receipts retain their original execution origin; only missing repair/hypothesis checks were newly executed in focused_validation.py.

problems.title: The cubic method requires a regularization condition and a computable stopping rule
problems.location: Equation (113), p. 2200; Theorem 13 and Remark 5, pp. 2201–2202
problems.check: Let f=x^2/2+K log(cosh x), K=10/(tanh(2)-4 sech^2(2))>0. It is 1-strongly convex with Hessian Lipschitz constant 4K/(3sqrt(3))=11.29693.... With cubic M=1, the unique model minimizers send 2 to -2 and back, exactly.
problems.result: M>0 alone does not imply the cited convergence. The restart theorem remains conditional on (114); its negative/undefined log at an already solved start and stopping test involving f* need qualification.
problems.correction: State appropriate M, e.g. M>=H_f for the majorizing cubic model, and the hypotheses of each imported rate. Start with an already-in-Q_f case and, with a known lower bound, give a preset stage count or computable certificate.
problems.counterevidence: The halving induction, geometric sum and exponents 1/4,1/6,1/7 under (114) are not refuted.

independent_check.decision: Upheld as regularization and observable-stop specification
independent_check.source_claim: After (113), mere M>0 is associated with the cubic convergence rate; Theorem 13 itself assumes rate (114).
operative_assumptions_verified: The even f=x^2/2+K*log(cosh x) has f''>=1 and globally Lipschitz Hessian with bound H_f=4K/(3sqrt(3)).
K=10/(tanh(2)-4*sech(2)^2)>0: e^4>19 implies tanh(2)>0.9 and positivity of the denominator.
M=1 satisfies the printed M>0 condition; the cubic model is strongly convex and its stationary point is its unique minimizer.
independent_check.decisive_independent_reasoning: At x=2 and h=-4, the derivative of the M=1 model is f'(2)-4*f''(2)-8=K*(tanh(2)-4*sech(2)^2)-10=0. Evenness produces the reverse step, so the iterates cycle between 2 and -2. The stated strong-convexity and Lipschitz-Hessian assumptions hold, yet arbitrary positive M does not give the imported convergence. The conditional restart calculation still yields exponents 1/4,1/6,1/7; an initial point already in Q and a stop involving unknown f* require explicit handling.
independent_check.counterevidence_and_limits: This does not refute Theorem 13 under its assumed rate (114). The external accelerated-rate theorems were not independently reacquired or universally validated. A known lower bound permits a predetermined sufficient stage count.
independent_check.severity_reason: The false generality is in the specification of the imported method/rate and stopping procedure; the conditional halving theorem and comparison exponents remain intact.
independent_check.repair_check: M>=H_f suffices to majorize for the displayed cubic model; require the proper hypotheses of every imported rate, handle an already-in-Q start, and use a preset stage count or observable certificate.

limitations: The exact acquired publisher PDF was reviewed; no alternate version or subsequent correction was compared.

The initial reviewer recorded reading all 41 source text pages and viewing all 41 source page images. Current focused acceptance read 36 listed text pages and viewed 15 listed source images; these origins are kept separate.
The acquired manifest contains two payload files: the original PDF and publisher metadata. Mechanical inventory verification is not scientific reading.
No author code or standalone supplement was acquired in the bounded source search. Their absence is not a mathematical defect.

The initial reviewer's examples and historical Python/SymPy/mpmath executions remain attributed to that reviewer. This independent executor rederived the decisive arguments and newly executed only the separately recorded missing repair/hypothesis checks.
The interval-barrier lower bound is analytic. The 100-digit PFS runs corroborate it and are not substituted for the proof.

External cited results and literature priority claims were not all independently fetched or verified. The comparison with cited accelerated methods remains conditional on their stated rate (114) and appropriate algorithm parameters.

Focused independent acceptance of the reported Problems is complete; this is not complete formal verification or human adjudication. Scientific decision remains pending and human_reviews remains empty.
